claims.how: Portia fimbriata principal eye resolves 12.4 cycles per degree, as calculated in the record.
Phidippus johnsoni resolves about 3.8 cycles per degree, from an inter-receptor angle of 0.13 degrees.
The principal retina's field is about 2 degrees wide and 21 degrees high in Phidippus johnsoni, drawn as a strip.
The side eyes respond only to movement, so still things are blind in the picture; the strength is set to full.

quotes.quote: The highest spatial frequency that can be recon- structed by layer 1 with minimum receptor-row spacing 1.4 J..Lm and distance 1,980 J..Lm from the posterior nodal point of the telephoto system is 1,980/2.8 = 710 rad- 1.
with more typical species (e.g., *Phidippus johnsoni*) having eyes that support visual angles of around 0.13 degrees (Blest, McIntyre, & Carter, 1988 ; Land, 1969).
the angular subtense of the retinae in object space (about 21 ° x 2° for layers 1 and 2) is the same in both species
